newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi says not worried about Lira rate.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi says not worried about Lira rate.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Wednesday that he was not worried about the lira and denied that he had said the currency had become too strong.
"The lira gives no cause for worry either today or yesterday," he told reporters.
"I did not say that yesterday," Prodi said referring to reports that he told journalists on Tuesday that the lira had become too strong.
"I made some observations about the past trends of the lira. I think that my comments were absolutely misunderstood," Prodi said.

The lira was trading at around 983.90 to the German mark at 1625 GMT on Wednesday, above the central parity of 990 to the mark at which it was readmitted to Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM) last November.
"We set an exchange rate of 990 and we are at 984. The lira can go to 960 or it can go to 1,000. So really we are always in this range," he said. --Rome newsroom +396-678-2501
